_comment: Which Deep Research build this repository expects. The pattern is
Upstream_Deeptutor's openmaic-pin.json: the sibling is built from our own
repository, so this names the fork commit our work sits on, the upstream
commit it is level with, and the image a deploy actually runs.
A commit says what the source was; only an image says what ran. `image.tag`
is a local build until the first image is published to a registry, at which
point `image.digest` is filled in and is the thing a deploy pulls.
Updating is a decision, not a surprise: check_research_ui_contract.py compares
a checkout's HEAD against `fork.commit` and reports the distance. It reports;
it does not force the move. Bump `fork.commit` and `verified` only after the
image builds and the frame still honours ?embed, ?lang and ?theme.

fork.note: Not a GitHub fork, on purpose: a repository GitHub classes as a fork does not run Actions until someone enables them by hand, and upstream's workflow triggers name upstream's branches. Every commit descends from AnotiaWang/deep-research-web-ui's real history, and the `upstream` remote is how a rebase reaches it.

upstream.note: fork/main descends from upstream d981f9c with 5 fork commits on top (?embed/?lang/?theme + Thai locale; server-side locale schema and prompt map taught Thai; inherited Docker Hub and nightly-sync workflows replaced by a GHCR publish; SearXNG as a web search provider) as of 2026-09-21

image.note: Published by the fork's image.yml on push to main; the digest is in that run's summary. This is what a deploy pulls. The package is private until its visibility is set to public in GitHub, after which it pulls without a login.
